Subject: Refine the supplied Rift Skitter into a 1.2 m tall fast melee creature. Keep the recognizable tall wedge-shaped head and dark armored chitin identity, but simplify the scratched surface noise into smooth large panels. Exactly FOUR walking legs: two front and two hind legs, radially attached beneath a compact central torso; NO arms or additional appendages. Each leg has three visibly articulated substantial segments and a compact pointed ground-contact foot. All four feet must be individually visible and spaced apart. Short raised neck, single sweeping central head crest, two tiny coral eyes, dark navy carapace with restrained teal in recessed flexible joints. Front legs can sweep forward for a lunge attack. Keep a low stable support polygon and visible gaps between head, torso, and upper limbs.
candidates.visual_review: Four distinct feet and articulated legs are visible. Crest retains the existing Skitter identity. Back-leg hip connections remain partly occluded and need top/back views.

weapon.name: Needlecrest energy carbine

views.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: isolated enemy energy carbine reconstruction reference, one object.
Input image: approved Rift Marksman Needlecrest, MATERIAL AND SHAPE LANGUAGE reference ONLY. Do NOT render the character or any hand.
Design one compact 0.65 meter long two-handed alien energy carbine for this character. Single coherent solid object with broad clean angular forms, navy central mechanism, warm pale ceramic outer panels, small muted teal inset, ONE tiny coral energy aperture at the muzzle. Two thick upper/lower forward ceramic shrouds partially enclose a short circular emitter; no bullet barrel, magazine, scope, sights, loose cable, floating pieces or many tiny details. Rear has a short robust shoulder pad; an angled navy primary pistol grip with spacious open trigger guard beneath the rear-middle body; ahead of it a broad integral lower fore-end for the support hand. Make both hand-grip regions clearly usable by three thick fingers and one thumb. No human hands or hand silhouettes. The primary and support grips are physically separated. Materials match the reference creature, subtle wear, mostly quiet surfaces.
Camera: exact orthographic LEFT SIDE elevation, muzzle points image LEFT, shoulder pad at RIGHT. Weapon horizontal, whole silhouette comfortably in frame, NO three-quarter view. Plain opaque light-gray studio background, even diffuse light, crisp silhouette, realistic PBR concept render. No text, labels, dimensions, watermark or cast shadows obscuring contours. ONE weapon only, not a collage.

Use case: identity-preserve. Input 1 is the exact left SIDE of an alien energy carbine; input 2 is its muzzle-end FRONT elevation. Generate the physically consistent exact TOP elevation of this SAME weapon, looking straight vertically down. Muzzle points LEFT, buttstock RIGHT. CRITICAL: the two pale muzzle shrouds are stacked VERTICALLY (one above and one below), NOT two side-by-side prongs. From directly above ONLY the SINGLE continuous broad upper ceramic muzzle shroud is visible; it hides the lower shroud and circular emitter. Do not expose the red muzzle lens from this overhead camera. Show one solid pale upper nose cap, navy central upper housing, pale upper receiver plates, narrow rear neck, and short shoulder stock. Preserve the weapon length, width based on end elevation, material layout, and design. Lower grip loops are occluded by body from this top camera. ONE object only, full horizontal weapon in frame, no text, no collage, no extra parts, plain opaque light-gray background, even lighting and crisp PBR materials.

Use case: identity-preserve. Image 1 is the exact energy carbine design to preserve. Create one additional production reference of that same 0.65 m weapon. Preserve every major shape, two grip openings, primary pistol grip, short shoulder stock, navy/pale ceramic/teal materials and coral muzzle, with same proportions. Change ONLY the camera. Exact orthographic FRONT end elevation looking straight into the muzzle aperture along the weapon's long axis. The small circular coral emitter centered between upper/lower pale shrouds, laterally symmetric body behind it. The grips extend below the body on centerline. Strong foreshortening: do NOT show the long side of the gun. Muzzle facing viewer, no yaw. ONE isolated weapon, full silhouette uncropped, opaque light-gray studio background, even neutral lighting, crisp realistic PBR materials, no character, no hands, no text, no labels, no collage, no watermark, no transparency.

weapon.rigging: Separate rigid object; primary pistol grip, support foregrip and central muzzle socket. See weapon/brief.md.

rift_skitter.finding: Five views preserve a four-legged Shieldback with separate paired hip sockets, broad shell, navy/teal regions and pale joints. Front correction reduces the rear-foot baseline mismatch.
rift_skitter.limits: Front/rear retain mild elevation and the stance is not pixel-calibrated across views. Top view resolves front/hind attachment order; use overall height and anatomical symmetry rather than tracing rear-leg perspective shortening.
rift_skitter.rig: Rigid shell and leg plates; four custom leg chains, one per hip socket. No humanoid rig. Foot contacts and shell clearance require Blender pose tests.

rift_marksman.finding: Four views preserve the split crest, humanoid proportions, navy chest plates, teal torso and empty hands. Side view clarifies the three-finger-plus-thumb hand.
rift_marksman.limits: Small panel seams and curled digits vary in visibility. Enforce three fingers plus one thumb on BOTH hands in the mesh; do not infer a missing digit from occlusion.
rift_marksman.rig: Humanoid anatomical rig adjusted to alien proportions; rigid plates with flexible joints. Separate weapon; attach to primary hand and use support-hand IK.

forge_bulwark.finding: Four views preserve two crown fins, two massive arms/legs and circular front core. Back view establishes torso-mounted crown supports, without an invented rear core.
forge_bulwark.limits: Rear support bridge shape is inferred from the approved front concept. Static images do not prove crown/shoulder/forearm clearance during an overhead slam.

rift_ray.finding: Five views preserve two thick crescent fins, one central tail, navy dorsal shell, pale belly and coral face. Top and side clarify planform and body depth.
rift_ray.limits: Front and back retain an elevated angle; they are appearance aids, not calibrated elevations. Tail foreshortening varies. Fin-rim segmentation is not consistently visible in generated views: keep root shell rigid and segment the pale rim when modeling, as specified in the brief.
rift_ray.rig: Custom body/fin/tail skeleton. Smooth fin-tissue weights; rigid shell segments. Test fin extremes and banking; do not rubber-warp a continuous ceramic rim.
